summary: Radar for 5 Nov 2026, all within the GLP-1 focus and ranked for Lane A watch time. The strongest bets are still the practical tirzepatide evergreens, and three of them have fresh hooks this week. (1) Thanksgiving on tirzepatide has risen across 10 snapshots in a row (momentum 78→84). Its search peak is Nov 18–27, so Shorts that feed the Thanksgiving long-form should start now. (2) Injection site reactions has the best-starting body-worry Short so far (223 views by day 2) and is the next long-form. (3) Stopping tirzepatide got a new hook on Nov 4 from Amgen's piece on the gap between prescriptions and persistence and from EMJ's aftercare warning. (4) Fatigue and dehydration are still queued long-forms. Cold and flu season makes dehydration timely and opens an emerging sick-day angle, which needs a strict 'no dose changes, ask your prescriber' framing because most blog results tell readers to delay their injection. News hooks this week: Lilly's Nov 5 release on ACR Convergence data, which covers the TOGETHER-PsA trial (tirzepatide plus ixekizumab vs ixekizumab alone in psoriatic arthritis with obesity) and retatrutide knee-osteoarthritis Phase 3 data. That fits the 13:00 tirzepatide-first and retatrutide 'what's confirmed' lanes. Also new: the Wegovy pill's Australian TGA approval (Guardian, Nov 4), useful for AU viewers, and the prediabetes story, now peaking in Reuters and US News. That one is best reframed around the randomized SURMOUNT-1 three-year prediabetes result, not the observational AHA study. ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) is a watch item for full REDEFINE 4 tirzepatide head-to-head data, but the topline dates from Feb 2026 and I couldn't confirm the presentation slot. Lower-priority candidates, marked caution: thiamine and Wernicke's after prolonged vomiting (2026 case reports; frame as 'when vomiting isn't normal'), the GLP-1 vs insulin cancer-risk link (observational, type 2 diabetes only), the Stanford 'natural Ozempic' story (BRP was published in Nature in 2025 and tested only in mice; myth-check angle only), and the poison-center call surge (no dosing content allowed). Rejected: online and research-peptide retatrutide sales, peptides imported from China, the 'dangerous turn for teens' piece, generic semaglutide in Brazil, and price-cut, cost and coverage stories.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? candidates.angle: An honest, encouraging answer: what the randomized withdrawal trial showed, why the body defends weight, and the habits linked to keeping results (protein, strength training, follow-up). Includes 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'. Persistence news is the fresh hook: many people stop early, so plan the conversation with your prescriber.

candidates.predicted_peak: steady; refreshed now, rising again after New Year (Jan 1–20)
candidates.why_now: Fresh Nov 4 coverage of how many people stop (Amgen) and how little aftercare they get (EMJ). It's the #2 redo in this week's playbook, and the earlier attempt was lost to narration defects.
